fact: Amnesty International says Addis Standard managing editor Million Beyene was abducted by national intelligence agency members on 15 April 2026 and held two weeks without access to his lawyer or family, which it says appears linked to his journalism.

Human Rights Watch reports the Ethiopian Media Authority permanently suspended two Deutsche Welle correspondents, alleging noncompliance with media and hate speech laws, after a nine-correspondent suspension from 23 October 2025.
OONI data shows Ethiopia blocked access to Facebook, Telegram, TikTok and YouTube from 9 February 2023, with the blocks apparently lasting until 17 July 2023.
Access Now says new internet shutdowns in Tigray, Ethiopia, are raising fears that the population cut off for over two years during the civil war will be disconnected again.
Access Now lists Ethiopia among 15 African countries where internet shutdowns were implemented in 2025.

CPJ reports that on 2 November 2026 the Ethiopian Media Authority suspended the registration of The Reporter's publisher indefinitely, covering its Amharic and English editions and digital platforms, for reports it said undermine national interests.

CPJ reports that two days before the 2 November 2026 suspension The Reporter published an editorial, 'Press Freedom Is Not A Luxury!', criticising authorities for treating independent reporting as a national security threat and calling for release of journalists held without charge.
Freedom House reports localised connectivity restrictions continued in Amhara Region, citing Addis Standard's February 2026 report of phone and internet outages in North Shewa Zone.

Freedom House reports Ethiopian authorities revoked independent digital outlet Addis Standard's licence in February 2026, citing CPJ, and an Addis Standard editor was seized from its newsroom in April 2026.

CIVICUS Monitor reports that on 22 May 2025 a Fafen Zone court sentenced Jigjiga Television Network founder Ahmed Awga to two years under the 2020 anti-hate speech law after he aired an interview alleging police brutality.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that Harari editor Muhyidin Abdullahi Omar was arrested on 5 April 2025 and charged on 28 April with defamation and disinformation over Facebook posts alleging corruption.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that journalist Tesfalem Waldyes was arrested on 8 June 2025 in Addis Ababa and accused by police of spreading false information.
CIVICUS Monitor reports that police arrested seven Ethiopian Broadcasting Service journalists on 26-28 March 2025 over an aired episode and accused them of inciting conflict.
Global Voices cites Ethiopia's Zone 9 bloggers as prosecuted for their posts in 2014.
